commands.summary: Record the human's approval of the brief, bound to its text; refused while `brief check` has blockers

validators.description: `--relayed-via` records a human's answer on behalf of an agent: a role is declared, with `--as` or the `CANON_ROLE` variable.
rejects: canon brief approve add-login --approver alice --note ok --relayed-via ask --actor impl --digest add-login=sha256:0123456789abcdef

validators.description: A relayed approval names the agent that recorded it: `--actor`, else the `CANON_ACTOR` variable, is given and is one word.
rejects: canon brief approve add-login --approver alice --note ok --relayed-via ask --as implementer --digest add-login=sha256:0123456789abcdef

validators.description: A relayed approval carries the human's own name and answer word for word: with `--relayed-via`, `--approver` and `--note` are not blank.
rejects: canon brief approve add-login --approver " " --note ok --relayed-via ask --as implementer --actor impl --digest add-login=sha256:0123456789abcdef
canon brief approve add-login --approver alice --note " " --relayed-via ask --as implementer --actor impl --digest add-login=sha256:0123456789abcdef

validators.description: The human's own answer (`--approver` and `--note`) is one line and, written by the human without `--relayed-via`, not blank once trimmed (a blank answer under `--relayed-via` is the relayed validator's, `USAGE`).
rejects: canon brief approve add-login --approver " " --note ok
canon brief approve add-login --approver alice --note " "

validators.description: A relayed approval names, for every change it approves, the digest the human was shown (`--digest <change>=sha256:<digest>`, once per change) and no digest of a change it does not approve. With no change operand the repo's only live change is read, and its digest is checked then.
rejects: canon brief approve add-login --approver alice --note ok --relayed-via ask --as implementer --actor impl
canon brief approve add-login --approver alice --note ok --relayed-via ask --as implementer --actor impl --digest add-login=sha256:0123456789abcdef --digest other=sha256:0123456789abcdef

validators.description: `--digest` names a change once: two entries for the same change must carry the same digest.
rejects: canon brief approve add-login --approver alice --note ok --relayed-via ask --as implementer --actor impl --digest add-login=sha256:aa --digest add-login=sha256:bb

order: `code` first. An optional member with no value is left out of the
document, so the body validates against the contract's error schema.

code.description: Stable SCREAMING_SNAKE code a caller branches on, registered in the tool's error registry.

details.description: Every error of an input that yields several, in the order the tool found them (spec 7.1.1); absent for one error.

expected.description: The valid values of `field`, when it takes a closed set.

field.description: The refused argv name (`--scenario`) or an RFC 6901 JSON pointer into `--input`.

hint.description: A working invocation or the next step.

reason.description: Which of the situations registered under `code` this is (since 1.1); registered in the code's row.

received.description: The value that was refused, with secrets redacted; `""` for an empty value the caller sent (1.1).

retryable.description: True only where running the same command again can succeed; equal to the registry row's.

suggestions.description: The nearest valid commands, options or values.

ErrorDetailBody.description: One item of `details` (spec 7.1.1): the members of [`ErrorBody`] except `retryable` and `details`.

ItemStatus.description: What happened to one element of a batch.

oneOf.description: The element ran and wrote.
The element ran and found its record already present with identical content.
The element ran and failed; `error` says why.
An earlier element failed, so this one never ran.

capabilityVersion.description:
SHA-256 hex content hash over the vocabulary this snapshot resolved
(module doc) — set by [`crate::resolve_snapshot::resolve_snapshot`],
empty on a hand-built [`CapabilitySnapshot::default`].

enums.description:
`enums.yaml`'s shared vocabulary, folded from every active plugin,
resolved by `Type::Domain(name)`.

evidenceKinds.description: `Type::Evidence`'s policy-resolved kind domain (D4) — see module doc.

inactive.description:
Installed-but-inactive directive tag -> owning plugin id (plugin
§11.2 fix-it parity; `crate::checker` surfaces this the same way
`check_directive` does, minus the LSP fix-it object itself since no
LSP consumes it yet).

CelSurface.description:
One record kind's CEL binding surface (S13 5.1/5.2/5.3, design D6):
every field a `policy.yaml` CEL expression bound to this kind may
reference off the `record` variable, plus the fixed pure-function
allowlist — folded in verbatim from the SAME `canon_policy::bindings_for`
call `canon-policy`'s own write-time validator uses (`canon-policy`
lib.rs's own forward reference: "S12's `resolve_surface`/
`ContextReport` gain a `policy` section populated by
`bindings::bindings_for`"), so this can never disagree with what a
`policy.yaml` CEL expression is actually checked against — invariant 2,
extended to the CEL surface.

fields.description:
`record.<field>` → that field's statically-resolved `CelType`,
rendered via `CelType`'s own `Display` (`BindingSet::field_names()`
over `BindingSet::record_fields`, never a hand-typed field list).

functions.description:
The allowlisted, non-macro callable functions
(`BindingSet::callable_function_names()`), each rendered via
`Display for FunctionSig` (`name(args) -> returns`) — excludes
CEL-native macros like `has` (`callable_function_names()`'s own
doc: the parser rewrites a well-formed `has(...)` call away before
it ever reaches the validator as a `Call`).

CommandSurface.description: One command a caller may run: a leaf of the generated spec, compact.

command.description: The canonical space-separated path, e.g. `evidence add`.

roles.description: The roles whose steps use the command; empty means humans only.

ContextReport.description:
The full authoring surface (design D3): everything an agent needs to
know BEFORE writing a canon artifact against this repo. Every map is a
`BTreeMap`; every array is sorted or built from an already-sorted
source (invariant 3).

cel.description:
S13 5.1/5.2/5.3 (design D6): by the same kind names, the SAME
key set `kinds` uses — the CEL binding surface (`record.<field>`
types + allowlisted functions) `policy.yaml`'s own write-time
validator checks a CEL expression against, never a second
independently-derived projection (invariant 2).

commands.description:
Every leaf of the command spec (filtered to the `--as` role's leaves
when one is given), sorted by command.

enums.description:
By enum type name (the schema registry's own `$defs` — never a
hand-maintained second list); each value is that enum's sorted
member set.

joinKeys.description:
By join-spine key name (S1's `join_spine_doc::rows()`) → that key's
grammar string.

kinds.description:
By the one name every surface uses ([`RecordKind::as_str`]): every
`RecordKind::ALL` member.

vocab.description:
S10 part2's typed authoring vocabulary (design.md D3, task 6.1) —
canon-vocab's own resolved directive/enum/evidence-kind index,
never a second hand-projected view of it (invariant 2).

ContextReport.title: ContextReport

EvidenceBindingSurface.description:
`experimental.evidence_binding`, keyed like `policy.yaml` (`case`,
`lane`, `scope`; each empty means unfiltered). Untagged like
[`SpecCoverageSurface`].

FamilySurface.description:
One artifact family (the files under `spec/`: ledger, divergences,
inventory, feature provenance, policy) and the record kinds that share its
name.

recordKinds.description: The record kinds (as `--kind` names them) whose wire name is this family's.

schema.description: The family's JSON Schema, next to the record kinds' schemas.

KindSurface.description:
One record kind's authoring shape: the fields an agent must supply, the
partition it lands in, and its current schema version.

envelopeFields.description:
Every top-level field name this kind's record carries (envelope
fields `schema`/`kind`/`at`/`actor` flattened alongside the kind's
own business fields — `#[serde(flatten)]` puts them all in the same
JSON object, so "envelope fields" for authoring purposes means the
whole top-level shape) mapped to whether it is required.

schema.description: The kind's JSON Schema, relative to the repository root of canon itself.

schemaVersion.description:
This kind's CURRENT format generation, read straight from
[`canon_model::RecordKind::schema_version`] — never a
hand-maintained copy, so `canon context` can never advertise a
generation no writer stamps (`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`).

Literal.description:
A record field's literal value (plugin §7 lineage, from the donor manifest
layer's types): the runtime shape [`type_accepts`] judges an authored
YAML value against a declared [`Type`]. `Map` carries `evidence`'s
`{kind, ref}` structure (and any other future record-shaped attr).

PartitionLayout.description:
The name layout one record kind's files follow in every store —
design D3's `partition: LayoutDescriptor`, built from
[`RecordKind::partition_template`] (canon-model's component table — never
a second, hand-written layout table).

PolicyFieldSurface.description:
One `policy.yaml` field's authoring-time shape: either a fixed value or
a CEL predicate's source (never its evaluated result — [`resolve_surface`]
has no specific artifact to evaluate against, only the repo's resolved
policy shape, matching invariant 1's "describes what CAN be authored").

value.description: The fixed value (the value itself is a [`serde_json::Value`] in memory; its schema is [`PolicyFlatValue`]).

PolicyFlatValue.description: What a fixed `policy.yaml` field can be: a flag, a count, a ratio or a name (a trust level).

PolicySurface.description:
`canon_gate::PolicyResolution`'s own fields, summarized field-by-field
via [`PolicyFieldSurface`] — one Rust field per `PolicyResolution` field,
so the mapping between "what the gate resolved" and "what context shows"
stays traceable by name, never a re-derived shape.

clean.description:
`PolicyResolution::is_clean()` — whether `policy.yaml` loaded with
zero problems for this repo.

diagnostics.description:
`PolicyDiagnostic::to_string()` per problem `resolve()` recorded,
in the order `resolve()` encountered them (deterministic per repo
state, matching invariant 3 — this is never sorted, since it is
already reproducible byte-for-byte on an unchanged repo).

spec_coverage.description:
s44's opt-in spec-corpus requirement. `None` (JSON `null`) = the
section is absent, which is a DIFFERENT fact from
`require_evidence: false` and stays distinguishable here: an
author needs to see whether the repo opted in at all.

RequireAuditSurface.description:
`spec_coverage.require_audit` in the `policy` section, keyed like
`policy.yaml` (0.15 D3). `scope` is the resolved status list (the
default `[verifying, shipped]` when the key is omitted); empty means
every scenario.

RequireReviewSurface.description:
`spec_coverage.require_review` in the `policy` section, keyed like
`policy.yaml`. `scope` is the resolved status list (the default
`[verifying, shipped]` when the key is omitted); empty means every
scenario.

ReviewRequirementSurface.description: The same requirement in the camelCase `review` section.

ReviewSurface.description:
The review vocabulary (issue #2): what `canon finding` and `canon
review` accept, and whether this repo requires review before a
subject is claimed done. Static vocabulary plus the resolved policy;
never a corpus read (invariant 1).

findingSeverities.description: `canon finding add --severity` values, in blocking order.

requireReview.description:
`spec_coverage.require_review`. `None` = not required here
(absent, or `spec_coverage` itself is absent or invalid).

reviewFields.description:
The `review` kind's fields → required, the SAME map
`kinds.review.envelopeFields` carries.

require_audit.description: Omitted when the sub-section is absent.

SpecCoverageSurface.description:
`spec_coverage`, keyed like `policy.yaml`. Serialized untagged: an
active section is its fields; a present-but-unusable one is
`{"invalid": "<detail>"}`.

VocabularySurface.description:
canon-vocab's own resolved capability snapshot (design.md D3, S10 part2
task 6.1): folded in verbatim from the SAME `canon_vocab::resolve_snapshot`
call the checker itself resolves against — no second, independently
re-derived projection of the typed authoring vocabulary (invariant 2).
`profile` is always `None` (the project's own `defaultProfile`, or
`"default"` with no `canon.project.yaml` at all) — `canon context` has
no `--profile` flag of its own yet; a future one would thread straight
through `resolve_surface`'s existing `(repo, opts)` shape without
touching this struct.

diagnostics.description:
`canon_vocab::checker::Diagnostic` (plugin load/activation
problems the resolution itself hit — a malformed
`canon.project.yaml`, an unresolvable `depends` range),
stringified one-per-entry in resolution order — mirrors
`PolicySurface::diagnostics`'s own "already reproducible
byte-for-byte on an unchanged repo" reasoning, never sorted.

snapshot.description:
The resolved directive/enum/evidence-kind index a typed task-atom
or handoff-body file is checked against right now — the exact
value `crate::gate`'s typed evidence path (task 4.4) re-resolves
fresh at gate time for the identical reason (Risks section: policy
is the live source of truth, never an authoring-time snapshot).

StrategyRef.description:
A full content SNAPSHOT of one retrieved strategy (S8 design D2),
never a live pointer: `strategy_id` names its source
`canon-learn::StrategyItem` for provenance only — `title`/`content`
are copied by value at the moment they were shown to an agent, so a
later edit or demotion of the source strategy can never retroactively
change what a [`Run`]'s [`Run::injected_guidance`] already recorded
(the "replay reproduces byte-identical run inputs" guarantee this
type exists to make possible). Deliberately NOT a `CanonRecord`
itself — it only ever lives nested inside [`Run::injected_guidance`],
mirroring how [`crate::envelope::Actor`] composes into [`Envelope`]
without being one of the twelve closed record kinds itself.

Additive provenance metadata captured for a [`Run`]. Every nested
snapshot is copied by value so replay can identify the exact provider,
model, skill, context, and policy inputs used for dispatch.

StrategyRef.description:
A full content SNAPSHOT of one retrieved strategy (S8 design D2),
never a live pointer: `strategy_id` names its source
`canon-learn::StrategyItem` for provenance only — `title`/`content`
are copied by value at the moment they were shown to an agent, so a
later edit or demotion of the source strategy can never retroactively
change what a [`Run`]'s [`Run::injected_guidance`] already recorded
(the "replay reproduces byte-identical run inputs" guarantee this
type exists to make possible). Deliberately NOT a `CanonRecord`
itself — it only ever lives nested inside [`Run::injected_guidance`],
mirroring how [`crate::envelope::Actor`] composes into [`Envelope`]
without being one of the twelve closed record kinds itself.

BatchItem.description: One element of a batch, in input order.

data.description: The element's ordinary report: a `written` or `unchanged` element has one, a `failed` or `skipped` one has none.

error.description: The element's ordinary error, its `field` a pointer into the batch (`/2/scenario`).

ErrorBody.description:
The `error` member of a failure envelope. Field order is the document
order: `code` first. An optional member with no value is left out of the
document, so the body validates against the contract's error schema.

code.description: Stable SCREAMING_SNAKE code a caller branches on, registered in the tool's error registry.

details.description: Every error of an input that yields several, in the order the tool found them (spec 7.1.1); absent for one error.

expected.description: The valid values of `field`, when it takes a closed set.

field.description: The refused argv name (`--scenario`) or an RFC 6901 JSON pointer into `--input`.

hint.description: A working invocation or the next step.

reason.description: Which of the situations registered under `code` this is (since 1.1); registered in the code's row.

received.description: The value that was refused, with secrets redacted; `""` for an empty value the caller sent (1.1).

retryable.description: True only where running the same command again can succeed; equal to the registry row's.

suggestions.description: The nearest valid commands, options or values.

ErrorDetailBody.description: One item of `details` (spec 7.1.1): the members of [`ErrorBody`] except `retryable` and `details`.

Actor.description:
Who/what produced a record — structured, never a bare `by: String`
(design D2, the donor audit's biggest cross-family gap).

`role` is `Option` (S11 design D5, "actor backfill is best-effort
from adjacent fields; absent stays absent"): a migrated legacy
record whose only source field is a bare `by: "legacy-ci-machine"`
string carries no role information at all — `canon migrate` maps
that string to `agent_id` and leaves `role: null` rather than
guessing, so the field must be able to express "unknown", not just
"known". Every record canon itself originates still supplies a role
via [`Actor::new`]; only backfilled/migrated records use
[`Actor::new_unattributed`].

Change.description:
A change: the top of the join spine's `change_id` row (change ↔
tasks ↔ specs). `subject_ids` links an imported plan change to every
durable [`Subject`] it was adopted under (0.18 D4: a change may belong
to several subjects; per-task subjects are out of scope). It is a
plain `pub` field left empty by [`Change::new`] and appended to by
`canon-cli`'s `subject adopt` at adoption time (mirroring how
[`Session::project_key`] is set outside this crate), never derived
here. Skipped when empty, so an unadopted change carries no key.

# Old records
The ledger is append-only. A change written before 0.18 carries a
single `subject_id` string; it reads as a one-element `subject_ids`
([`one_or_many_subjects`]) and is never rewritten. Renaming the field
is a format generation change on a kind whose `at` can be byte-stable
(plan import), so [`RecordKind::Change`] is at schema `2`.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

MalformedEntry.description:
One structurally-broken construct a [`PlanAdapter::parse`] call
skipped (s18 `loud-plan-import-diagnostics` spec's "Every malformed
plan-import construct is named by path and reason"): a NAMED entry
carrying the construct's relative path and a reason drawn from a
fixed, per-adapter reason vocabulary — never an anonymous increment
to a bare count with no way to identify WHICH construct failed or
WHY. `hint` carries an additional actionable hint for a specific
near-miss signature (e.g. the openspec dialect's root-one-level-
too-high `changes`-basename hint) — `None` for every ordinary
malformed entry.

hint.description:
An additional actionable hint for a specific near-miss
signature — `None` for every ordinary malformed entry.

path.description:
The construct's path (relative to the source root when
derivable — never an absolute path leaking the host filesystem
layout into a persisted/printed diagnostic).

reason.description:
A stable reason string drawn from the adapter's own fixed
vocabulary (e.g. the openspec dialect's `"missing-proposal-md"`,
`"invalid-change-id-grammar"`, `"unreadable-directory"`).

PlanSourceSummary.description:
One configured source's contribution to a pass (human + `--json`
output, task 3.5: "per-source counts + drop diagnostics + malformed
tallies").

changesUnwritten.description:
Degraded to the `unwritten` seam (a routed tier unreachable/
unrouted) — the bodies themselves are in
[`PlansOutcome::unwritten_changes`]/`unwritten_tasks`.

cursorAdvanced.description:
`true` iff this source's watermark cursor was refreshed this
pass — `false` for a skipped-unchanged source (nothing to
refresh) AND for a (re-)parsed source with any unwritten
candidate (the pass was not fully durable).

duplicateChangeId.description:
`change_id`s this source lost to an EARLIER-configured source
this pass (design D8) — that `Change` and every `Task` under it
were skipped entirely, never persisted.

malformed.description:
Structurally-broken constructs the adapter itself skipped
(design D3) — distinct from `duplicate_change_id`, which this
driver (not the adapter) detects. Each one NAMED by path +
reason [+ hint] (s18 `loud-plan-import-diagnostics` spec) —
`.len()` is the scalar tally a caller that only needs the count
reaches for.

skippedUnchanged.description:
`true` iff the S3-generalized watermark gate skipped this
source wholesale (byte-identical to its cursor) — every other
field is `0`/empty in that case.

unmapped.description:
Per-construct NAMED unmapped-drop counts straight from the
adapter's [`PlanParseOutcome`] (design D3).

dryRun.description:
A `--dry-run` preview: nothing was persisted and no cursor moved;
the `*Persisted` counts are what a real pass would persist.

hotStore.description: Where the hot records go (0.30): the hot store's location; absent on a `--dry-run` or with no hot rung.

unwrittenChanges.description:
Every `Change`/`Task` a routed-but-unreachable (or wholly
unrouted) tier could not accept this pass — printed, never
silently dropped, never fatal to a sibling record whose tier
write already succeeded (spec "An unreachable pg tier degrades
to the unwritten seam").

RecordKind.description:
The fourteen closed record kinds `canon-model` recognizes (design D1;
`Subject` is the reviewed 13th kind, added by s36, and `Finding` the
reviewed 14th, added by s43 — the "a new kind is a reviewed, breaking
`canon-model` change" process design D1 mandates, exercised twice for
real). A fifteenth kind is again a reviewed, breaking
change — never a `kind: String` escape hatch (design D1's explicitly
rejected alternative: an untyped `payload: serde_json::Value` would
silently recreate the "no documented join key" problem inside canon
itself).

RoleId.description: kebab-case role slug (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), e.g. `implementer`, `reviewer` — joins: not a join-spine key; used by `Actor.role` and `regime_key`'s `<role>` segment

ScenarioId.description: `<area>.<surface>.<nn>` — `[a-z0-9-]+\.[a-z0-9-]+\.\d{2,}`; never renumbered once assigned — joins: spec ↔ test ↔ ledger ↔ divergence

SessionId.description: opaque, non-empty agent-CLI session token; derivation source varies by adapter (Claude Code/Codex: transcript filename stem; omp/pi: in-file header `id` field) — this type validates shape only, never a single fixed format — joins: session ↔ cost ↔ run ↔ trajectory

SubjectId.description: subject slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the durable product-unit identifier — joins: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario

Task.description:
A task within a change (join-spine `task_id` row: task ↔ evidence ↔
trajectory). `change_id` is never a separate field — `task_id`
already embeds it; use [`TaskId::change_id`] to decompose.

depends_on.description:
Optional, declaratively-authored DEPENDENCY references (s37
`execution-graph-topology`, subject `flywheel-execution-graph`)
— which sibling `Task`(s) in the SAME change this task's own
plan text declares it comes after. Populated ONLY from a
dependency expression the dialect's corpus demonstrably uses
(the openspec dialect's in-row `depends on <n>`/`after <n>`
marker prose; the superpowers dialect's `- Consumes: … from
Task <n>` interface line), never from a syntax invented for
canon's convenience and never from dotted-numbering nesting —
`<change>#6.2` does NOT implicitly depend on `<change>#6`. A
reference that fails to resolve to a real sibling row is
DROPPED with a named import diagnostic, never an import
failure, because prose is ambiguous and "malformed evidence is
no evidence".

DECLARED INTENT ONLY: canon never schedules, orders, blocks, or
executes anything from this field. It is the PLAN-side half of
the execution graph — the half s37's plan-vs-actual diff reads
against `Run.parent_run_id`'s OBSERVED dispatch lineage, which
is what makes a declared-but-never-honored ordering visible to
the reward flywheel at all.

Empty by default, mirroring [`Task::scenario_refs`]'s own
additive-field shape (and, like it, `skip_serializing_if` so an
empty vec never introduces a spurious key — every pre-s37
`Task` stays byte-identical on the wire, and its content digest
with it).

This field IS nonetheless what bumped `Task` to
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] `2`
(`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`), and NOT because the wire form
broke — it did not. A `Task`'s `Envelope.at` is
`file_modified_at(<source plan doc>)` (s20 D7), byte-stable so an
unchanged plan re-imports idempotently; adding this field changed
the PARSER, not the source document's mtime, so the stale and
fresh record for one `task_id` carry an IDENTICAL `at` and
`canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key` needs a generation signal
to order them. Without the bump it fell through to the
lexicographic digest tie-break and surfaced this field on an
arbitrary SUBSET of one file's rows. See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for why `Run`/`Handoff` gained
fields on the same branch and correctly stayed at `1`.

scenario_refs.description:
Optional, declaratively-authored scenario-coverage references
(design s20 Decision 1) — which `Scenario`(s) this task is
meant to satisfy, populated ONLY from an explicit `[covers:
…]` `tasks.md` segment, never inferred from prose. Empty by
default, mirroring `EvidenceRecord.surface_ref`'s own
additive-field shape; a `Task` with no declared refs is
byte-identical to a pre-s20 `Task` on the wire.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

TaskId.description: `<change_id>#<n>`, where `<n>` is one or more dot-separated integers (`1`, `1.1`, `6.2`) matching `tasks.md`'s own numbering — joins: task ↔ evidence ↔ trajectory

TaskStatus.description:
A `tasks.md` checkbox's canonical state — `Open` is the unchecked
`- [ ]`, `Done` the checked `- [x]`. `evidence_note` carries the
same "one-line evidence note" discipline this very change's own
tasks.md is held to — a `Done` task without one is a checkbox
overclaim, not evidence.

ArtifactAdapterSummary.description:
One registered adapter's contribution to this pass — mirrors
`crate::ingest::AdapterSummary`'s per-adapter shape, generalized
with a `status` field so a `Records`-source read failure is a
visible, distinct outcome (module doc's "documented seam"), never
collapsed into the same zero-events shape an unconfigured
`Path`-source adapter reports.

status.description:
`"read"` (this adapter's source was actually reached, whether
or not it was configured/had records) | `"unavailable"` (a
`Records`-source read failed before `parse` ever ran) |
`"disabled"` (a `native_verdict: true` entry, S15 P4, whose
`ArtifactSourceConfig::native_records` switch is off — never
`"unavailable"`, which is reserved for a genuine read failure).

convergenceConflicts.description:
Superseded copies this pass REFUSED to delete because they carry
a `verdict_record` or `run_id` the canonical row does not — s42
(`close-the-open-loops`) re-review (`ReviewRuns` finding 1). One
entry per kept row, ordered by regime key then by the kept row's
own id, so a repeat pass prints byte-identical lines.

Empty for every store this driver produced on its own, and for
every ordinary upgrade: the losing copies a pre-s38 pass appended
were never marked and never attributed, so they claim nothing.
A non-empty entry means two stored rows disagree about a fact
`canon strategy promote` reads (module doc), and the disagreement is
STANDING — it is re-reported every pass until an operator removes
the row they judge wrong, because this driver will not pick for
them.

dryRun.description:
A `--dry-run` preview: nothing was written; the counts are what a
real pass would do (convergence of superseded copies is not previewed).

hotStore.description: Where the hot records go (0.30): the hot store's location; absent on a `--dry-run` or with no hot rung.

strategyItemsRebuilt.description:
Sum of every regime's freshly-distilled `StrategyItem` count
([`NamespaceConvergence::items`]) — the count that actually lands
in `stg_strategy_items`, i.e. what makes S9's `mart_role_memory`
non-empty.

trajectoriesConvergedDeleted.description:
Raw `Trajectory` rows this pass DELETED as this driver's own
superseded copies whose independently-written provenance the
canonical row also carries ([`RawConvergence::deletable`]) — s42
(`close-the-open-loops`).

Reported rather than left silent, on the same "reported, never
silent" discipline every other degrade and skip in this outcome
follows. It is the only counter here that names bytes that no
longer exist, so an operator seeing it non-zero should read the
module doc's account of what a deleted row makes unresolvable. It
is non-zero at most ONCE per namespace per upgrade: a namespace a
post-s38 canon produced on its own has no superseded copies to
remove, and one converging pass empties an upgraded one of every
copy it is allowed to remove — the rest are reported in
[`ArtifactIngestOutcome::convergence_conflicts`] and never
counted here.

trajectoriesLeftPending.description:
Trajectories deliberately LEFT `Pending`: the role's own
`RewardFn` resolved to [`VerdictOutcome::Pending`], which
`mark_trajectory_verdict` rejects outright
([`canon_learn::LearnError::CannotMarkVerdictPending`]) because
`Pending` is the unset default, never a covering-verdict write.
The `dev` role reaches this legitimately: `compute_dev_reward`'s
additive triad stays `Pending` below a full `1.0` (a partial
`pr-merged` + `ci-pass` without `no-rollback`), waiting for the
S7 webhook receiver's no-rollback timer to resolve it. Counted,
never an error.

trajectoriesMarked.description:
Trajectories whose covering verdict+reward was RESOLVED and
written back in this same pass
([`canon_learn::RewardRegistry::compute_for_trajectory`] +
[`canon_learn::mark_trajectory_verdict`]). Every freshly
constructed `Trajectory` starts `VerdictOutcome::Pending` (S7
design D2's two-phase reward-write model), and S7's promotion
gates read `verdict_record.outcome`, NOT the raw `verdicts`
list — so a trajectory left `Pending` is invisible to
`OccurrencePromotionGate`/`CrnPromotionGate` and can never
corroborate a promotion. This counter is what makes the
artifact-ingest half of the flywheel observable.

trajectoriesSkippedDuplicate.description:
A trajectory whose FULL identity (identity-shape version +
`regime_key` + ordered `VerdictRow` contents + the rendered
`task`/`context`) already matches a trajectory this exact
`regime_key` holds ([`trajectory_content_digest`]) — skipped and
counted (module doc's write-time idempotence), never a
double-write of an unchanged corpus. A row whose verdict set
matches but whose TEXT does not is not this: it is superseded in
place, see [`PersistedTrajectory::superseded`].

trajectoriesSkippedUnregisteredRole.description:
A trajectory whose `regime_key` role is not registered in this
repo's `canon_learn::RoleRegistry` (`canon.yaml` `learn.roles`,
or the built-in set) — skipped and counted (module doc's
"documented seam"), never a fatal error for the rest of the
batch.

BatchIngestRecordsReport.description:
`Batch<Name>Report`: the `data` of a leaf run with a JSON array or NDJSON as `--input`.
`R` is the leaf's ordinary report; the binary itself carries each element's report as JSON.

nextOmitted.description: How many further `meta.next` steps were left out past the limit

unchanged.description: true when a repeat found its work already done with identical content and wrote nothing; absent otherwise

waitingOn.description: With a declared role: how many steps each other owner holds (`human` for the steps only the human takes)

BatchIngestRecordsReport.title: BatchReport

BatchItem.description: One element of a batch, in input order.

data.description: The element's ordinary report: a `written` or `unchanged` element has one, a `failed` or `skipped` one has none.

error.description: The element's ordinary error, its `field` a pointer into the batch (`/2/scenario`).

ConvergenceConflict.description:
One superseded copy the raw convergence KEPT rather than deleted,
because it carries an independently-written field the canonical row
does not (module doc, "The derivation key is NOT enough to authorize
that delete"). s42 (`close-the-open-loops`) re-review, `ReviewRuns`
finding 1.

A report, never a resolution. Both rows stay exactly as they are, so
`canon strategy promote` keeps reading the contradiction off
`query_by_regime_key` — which is the whole point: the alternative
this replaced silently deleted the loser and changed what the gate
saw.

canonicalId.description:
The row the smallest-id rule keeps
([`canonical_driver_row`]) — the one whose provenance the kept
row was compared against.

claims.description:
Every claim `retained_id` makes that `canonical_id` does not,
one line per disagreeing field in [`RowProvenance`]'s fixed field
order ([`RowProvenance::claims_beyond`]). Never empty — an empty
list IS the deletable case, and no conflict is constructed for it.

regimeKey.description: The namespace both rows sit under.

retainedId.description:
The superseded row that survived the delete. Still withheld from
the distiller exactly as s41 left it: kept is not served.

ErrorBody.description:
The `error` member of a failure envelope. Field order is the document
order: `code` first. An optional member with no value is left out of the
document, so the body validates against the contract's error schema.

code.description: Stable SCREAMING_SNAKE code a caller branches on, registered in the tool's error registry.

details.description: Every error of an input that yields several, in the order the tool found them (spec 7.1.1); absent for one error.

expected.description: The valid values of `field`, when it takes a closed set.

field.description: The refused argv name (`--scenario`) or an RFC 6901 JSON pointer into `--input`.

hint.description: A working invocation or the next step.

reason.description: Which of the situations registered under `code` this is (since 1.1); registered in the code's row.

received.description: The value that was refused, with secrets redacted; `""` for an empty value the caller sent (1.1).

retryable.description: True only where running the same command again can succeed; equal to the registry row's.

suggestions.description: The nearest valid commands, options or values.

ErrorDetailBody.description: One item of `details` (spec 7.1.1): the members of [`ErrorBody`] except `retryable` and `details`.

run.description: Attribute this pass's trajectories to a dispatched run (a RunId minted by `canon dispatch begin`)

RetrieveReport.description:
`--json`'s `data`: the raw guidance items as an array, each a
`StrategyRef` — the exact snapshot shape a caller would embed into
`Run::injected_guidance` verbatim (design decision 2), never a
human-table projection of it. An empty result is `[]`, never an
omitted/null value, so a caller piping `(.data // .)` into a manifest
write always gets a well-formed JSON array. The installed hook reads
`(.data // .)`, so it works with the 0.27 bare array and this envelope.
RetrieveReport.title: RetrieveReport

StrategyRef.description:
A full content SNAPSHOT of one retrieved strategy (S8 design D2),
never a live pointer: `strategy_id` names its source
`canon-learn::StrategyItem` for provenance only — `title`/`content`
are copied by value at the moment they were shown to an agent, so a
later edit or demotion of the source strategy can never retroactively
change what a [`Run`]'s [`Run::injected_guidance`] already recorded
(the "replay reproduces byte-identical run inputs" guarantee this
type exists to make possible). Deliberately NOT a `CanonRecord`
itself — it only ever lives nested inside [`Run::injected_guidance`],
mirroring how [`crate::envelope::Actor`] composes into [`Envelope`]
without being one of the twelve closed record kinds itself.

ApprovalRelay.description:
How an approval reached canon when an agent recorded it for a human
(0.32): the agent's declared role and actor, the tool the human was asked
with, and, where the record has no field of its own for them, the human's
name and answer. Written only for a relayed approval; a record without it
is the human's own.

actor.description: The agent's actor id.

answer.description: The human's answer as given, when the record holds it nowhere else.

approver.description: The human's name, when the record holds it nowhere else.

role.description: The role the recording agent declared (`--as` / `CANON_ROLE`).

tool.description: The tool the human was asked with (`ask`, `AskUserQuestion`, `chat`).

evaluator.description: The latest audit's evaluator, when there is one.

confirmed.description: Sampled scenarios whose latest audit is `confirmed`.

owed.description:
Sampled scenarios still owing an audit: none recorded, or the
latest is `indeterminate`.

refuted.description:
Every scenario whose latest audit is `refuted` (`false-success`),
sampled or not.

sampled.description:
In-scope scenarios `spec_coverage.require_audit` sampled (0 when
it is off).

BriefState.description: What a brief's approval reads as ([`BriefStatus::status`]).

oneOf.description: An `Approved:` line binds the brief's text (or predates digests).
No `Approved:` line, or no canon brief yet.
The brief changed after its approval.

BriefStatus.description:
Whether one adopted change records the human's approval of its brief: an
`Approved:` line in that change's canon `brief.md` (module doc). A fix
stays inside the approved change, so a newer adopted change is a new
scope, and an older change's approval does not cover it. One entry per
change the subject answers for ([`governing`]) is `canon status`'s
`briefs`.

brief.description:
That change's canon `brief.md`, relative to the repo root: the one
file the approval is read from. Omitted when the change has no
brief to answer (neither a canon `brief.md` nor an external
`proposal.md`).

briefExists.description:
Whether [`Self::brief`] exists. `false` for an external change
whose canon brief is still to be created, with a `Source:` line
naming [`Self::source`].

change.description:
The adopted change this entry judges, whose canon `brief.md` must carry
the approval. Omitted when the subject adopts no change.

enforced.description:
Whether the missing approval blocks (module doc): not approved,
and the change has a brief to answer. Then status
asks the human and the ship guard refuses; otherwise both only
report it.

findings.description:
What `canon brief check` found in the brief's text (0.19 D2):
filled by `canon status` only, for a brief in the PRD format.
Omitted for a pre-0.19 brief, which is read as before.

legacyApproval.description:
The approval line has no digest (pre-0.19): approved, but status
advises re-approving it so it binds to the brief's text.

reason.description:
Why the subject answers for this change ([`Reason`]); `None` for the
newest adopted change of a subject with no governing change.

relay.description:
Set when an agent recorded the approval for the human (0.32): the
`(relayed by …)` marker of the approval line, read back.

source.description:
The external plan document the change comes from: the `Source:`
line of the canon `brief.md`, or, before that file exists, the
external openspec `proposal.md` found under the plan sources.

ChangeId.description: openspec change slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the directory name under `openspec/changes/` — joins: change ↔ tasks ↔ specs

DanglingSummary.description:
How many references are unresolved, in all and per kind of reference
(`<record kind>.<field>`, e.g. `finding.change_id`).

FlowScenarioState.description:
One scenario covering a flow step, with the evidence and review state
the gate reads for it.

review.description:
`reviewed`, or the review gap's kind: `missing`, `stale`,
`unsigned`, `not-distinct`; `not-indexed` when the scenario index
has no record for the id yet (`canon inventory sync`).

FlowStep.description: One flow step of the brief and what covers it.

change.description: The change whose brief defines it.

gaps.description: `no scenario` and/or `no failure case`; empty when covered.

projectId.description: The `specs.roots[]` id the surface lives under.

level.description:
The policy's level (0.16 D3, [`crate::policy_level::detect`]):
`light`, `standard`, `strict`, or `custom`; `null` when the
policy is absent.

spec_coverage.description:
The effective `spec_coverage` section, keyed like `policy.yaml`
(the same shape `canon context --json` prints); `null` when absent.

Reason.description: Why a subject answers for an adopted change ([`governing`]).

oneOf.description: A scenario the subject owns is tagged `@flow:<change>.*`.

The change's brief carries an `Approved:` line (edited since or not),
whatever tags say.

The change is a chore: it has no scenario to tag, so it governs from
the moment it is adopted.

RequireAuditSurface.description:
`spec_coverage.require_audit` in the `policy` section, keyed like
`policy.yaml` (0.15 D3). `scope` is the resolved status list (the
default `[verifying, shipped]` when the key is omitted); empty means
every scenario.

RequireReviewSurface.description:
`spec_coverage.require_review` in the `policy` section, keyed like
`policy.yaml`. `scope` is the resolved status list (the default
`[verifying, shipped]` when the key is omitted); empty means every
scenario.

require_audit.description: Omitted when the sub-section is absent.

SpecCoverageSurface.description:
`spec_coverage`, keyed like `policy.yaml`. Serialized untagged: an
active section is its fields; a present-but-unusable one is
`{"invalid": "<detail>"}`.

StatusReport.description: The whole report, in the order it prints.

audits.description:
Audit obligations and refutations (0.15 D3). Omitted when
`require_audit` is off and no latest audit is refuted.

danglingReferences.description:
References of findings, evidence and subjects to a source nothing committed holds
(0.30 `record-links`), in all and per kind of reference. Absent when they were not
checked: a run that stopped early, or sources that could not be read (a warning says).

nextOmitted.description: How many further `meta.next` steps were left out past the limit

subjects.description: Lifecycle order (proposed → retired), then subject id.

unchanged.description: true when a repeat found its work already done with identical content and wrote nothing; absent otherwise

unowned.description: Scenario ids (latest generation) whose `@subject:` tag is absent.

waitingOn.description: With a declared role: how many steps each other owner holds (`human` for the steps only the human takes)

warnings.description:
One line per condition that makes the counts below incomplete or
the gate weaker than it looks.

StatusReport.title: StatusReport

acceptedDivergences.description:
Counted divergent scenarios a reviewer accepted as known gaps
(`canon divergence accept`) whose acceptance still holds, each as
`accepted-divergence <id> — <tracking> (expires <date>)`. They are
not in `divergent`; omitted when empty.

briefs.description:
The briefs the subject answers for (0.31): one entry per adopted
change that is tagged by one of its scenarios, has an `Approved:`
line, or is a chore, in adoption order, each with whether it reads as
approved, why it governs and what `canon brief check` found. A subject
with no such change has the one entry of its newest adopted change,
which its reopen, ship and evidence wait on for a first approval, with
no `reason` (or, adopting no change, an entry with no `change`).
Present for `building`, `verifying` and `shipped` subjects, and for a
`proposed` subject whose change has a brief to answer; omitted when
empty.

choreReviews.description: Approved chore changes with no qualifying change-level review (0.23 D5).

divergent.description: Counted scenarios whose latest verdict (for some role) is divergent.

evidenced.description: Counted scenarios with a ledger verdict.

excluded.description: Owned scenarios `exclude_lanes` removes from every count.

flow.description:
The flow steps of the briefs of every tagged change the subject answers
for, with the scenarios tagged `@flow:<change>.<F-id>` (0.19 D4, 0.31).
Omitted for a brief with no flow steps (a legacy brief) or no brief.

openBlockers.description: Open blocker findings on the subject's adopted changes.

pendingDrafts.description:
The adopted changes that are pending drafts ([`crate::brief::governing`]):
never approved, not a chore, and no scenario of the subject tagged
`@flow:<change>.*` for them, so reopen, evidence and ship do not read
them. Omitted when empty.

red.description:
For a `shipped` subject, what makes its gate red now (0.18 D3):
what the `verifying → shipped` guard would refuse it on
([`crate::subject::shipped_gate_gaps`], the same checks), one
phrase per failure class: `<n> <class> (first: <subject>)`.
Status then names the reopen command. Omitted when empty.

reviewDue.description:
Whether `require_review` covers this subject's status or the next
one on the chain, i.e. whether its reviews are due now.

reviewed.description:
Counted scenarios with a qualifying review under the
`require_review` rule (any current signed review when it is off).

staleReviews.description:
Counted scenarios whose only signed reviews are stale: pinned to a
spec or evidence that has since changed (0.15 D1).

unsignedReviews.description:
Counted scenarios whose latest reviews are all `indeterminate` or
`unavailable` (0.15 D4).

Actor.description:
Who/what produced a record — structured, never a bare `by: String`
(design D2, the donor audit's biggest cross-family gap).

`role` is `Option` (S11 design D5, "actor backfill is best-effort
from adjacent fields; absent stays absent"): a migrated legacy
record whose only source field is a bare `by: "legacy-ci-machine"`
string carries no role information at all — `canon migrate` maps
that string to `agent_id` and leaves `role: null` rather than
guessing, so the field must be able to express "unknown", not just
"known". Every record canon itself originates still supplies a role
via [`Actor::new`]; only backfilled/migrated records use
[`Actor::new_unattributed`].

RecordKind.description:
The fourteen closed record kinds `canon-model` recognizes (design D1;
`Subject` is the reviewed 13th kind, added by s36, and `Finding` the
reviewed 14th, added by s43 — the "a new kind is a reviewed, breaking
`canon-model` change" process design D1 mandates, exercised twice for
real). A fifteenth kind is again a reviewed, breaking
change — never a `kind: String` escape hatch (design D1's explicitly
rejected alternative: an untyped `payload: serde_json::Value` would
silently recreate the "no documented join key" problem inside canon
itself).

Reopen.description: A recorded reopen of a shipped subject (see [`Subject::reopen`]).

actor.description: Who reopened it.

change.description:
The approved change the follow-up work goes into: the subject's
newest adopted change when it reopened. Absent when it adopted
none.

reason.description: The operator's reason, verbatim (one line).

RoleId.description: kebab-case role slug (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), e.g. `implementer`, `reviewer` — joins: not a join-spine key; used by `Actor.role` and `regime_key`'s `<role>` segment

SessionId.description: opaque, non-empty agent-CLI session token; derivation source varies by adapter (Claude Code/Codex: transcript filename stem; omp/pi: in-file header `id` field) — this type validates shape only, never a single fixed format — joins: session ↔ cost ↔ run ↔ trajectory

StatusOverride.description:
A recorded waiver of the `spec_coverage.require_review` status guard
(see [`Subject::status_override`]). `canon gate check` reports a gap
as an advisory naming this waiver only when it matches one of
`waived` exactly, and only while the subject stays at `to`. A gap that
appears later (a new blocker, a newly tagged scenario) is not covered
and stays a violation.

actor.description: Who waived it.

reason.description: The operator's reason, verbatim (one line).

to.description: The status the transition moved to under this waiver.

waived.description: Exactly the guard violations this waiver let through, sorted.

actor.description: Who gave it.

reason.description: The operator's reason, verbatim (one line).

Subject.description:
A subject (join-spine `subject_id` row: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario)
— the durable product/management unit a team plans, designs, builds,
and measures across many changes (s36, the reviewed 13th kind). A
by-id kind like [`Change`]: flat Hive partition, no mandatory
`scenario_id`. `domain` is a validated-shape-only kebab slug (see
[`deserialize_domain_slug`] — the closed vocabulary lives in
`canon/vocab`, not here); `owner_role` names the accountable role;
`change_ids` accumulates as plan changes are adopted
(additive-empty by default, so a freshly-authored subject with no
links yet is still a valid, minimal record). One change may be listed
by several subjects (0.18 D4); the change's own
[`Change::subject_ids`] lists each of them, and readers join a
subject to its changes from both sides.

The scenario side of the join lives on [`Scenario::subject_id`], set
by `canon inventory sync` from each scenario's `@subject:<id>` tag —
the spec corpus is the one place that link is authored. A subject
carries no copy of it: a second, separately-written list is exactly
what drifted (never populated, so every reader saw zero scenarios and
the ship gate passed on an empty set). Records written before that
list was removed still deserialize; the stale key is ignored.

reopen.description:
Who reopened this subject from `shipped` to `verifying`, and why
(0.18 D3, `canon subject move <id> --to verifying --reason`). Set
only on the record that reopens; every other `canon subject
move` write clears it, like [`Self::status_override`]. Skipped
when absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

status_override.description:
The accountable waiver this record's status transition was let
through under, when `spec_coverage.require_review` refused it and
the operator passed `canon subject move --override-reason`.
Skipped when absent, so every subject written without one stays
byte-identical on the wire. Each `canon subject move` write
clears it and sets it again only when it waives something, so a
waiver never outlives the status it was granted for.

status_reason.description:
The note an operator gave the transition that wrote this record
(`canon subject move <id> --to <state> --reason`, 0.21.1), on
any transition; a reopen records it here too, next to
[`Self::reopen`]. Every `canon subject move` write clears it
and sets it again only when given a `--reason`. Skipped when
absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

SubjectStatus.description:
A `Subject`'s lifecycle (s36 design D1): the states a product unit
moves through, `proposed → specced → building → verifying → shipped
→ retired`. Transitions are policy-gated (CEL) at the CLI/gate layer
(s35 seam); this enum owns only the closed set and its stable

RecordKind.description:
The fourteen closed record kinds `canon-model` recognizes (design D1;
`Subject` is the reviewed 13th kind, added by s36, and `Finding` the
reviewed 14th, added by s43 — the "a new kind is a reviewed, breaking

real). A fifteenth kind is again a reviewed, breaking
change — never a `kind: String` escape hatch (design D1's explicitly
rejected alternative: an untyped `payload: serde_json::Value` would
silently recreate the "no documented join key" problem inside canon
itself).

StatusOverride.description:
A recorded waiver of the `spec_coverage.require_review` status guard
(see [`Subject::status_override`]). `canon gate check` reports a gap
as an advisory naming this waiver only when it matches one of
`waived` exactly, and only while the subject stays at `to`. A gap that
appears later (a new blocker, a newly tagged scenario) is not covered
and stays a violation.

actor.description: Who waived it.

reason.description: The operator's reason, verbatim (one line).

to.description: The status the transition moved to under this waiver.

waived.description: Exactly the guard violations this waiver let through, sorted.

actor.description: Who gave it.

reason.description: The operator's reason, verbatim (one line).

Subject.description:
A subject (join-spine `subject_id` row: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario)
— the durable product/management unit a team plans, designs, builds,
and measures across many changes (s36, the reviewed 13th kind). A
by-id kind like [`Change`]: flat Hive partition, no mandatory
`scenario_id`. `domain` is a validated-shape-only kebab slug (see
[`deserialize_domain_slug`] — the closed vocabulary lives in
`canon/vocab`, not here); `owner_role` names the accountable role;
`change_ids` accumulates as plan changes are adopted
(additive-empty by default, so a freshly-authored subject with no
links yet is still a valid, minimal record). One change may be listed
by several subjects (0.18 D4); the change's own
[`Change::subject_ids`] lists each of them, and readers join a
subject to its changes from both sides.

The scenario side of the join lives on [`Scenario::subject_id`], set
by `canon inventory sync` from each scenario's `@subject:<id>` tag —
the spec corpus is the one place that link is authored. A subject
carries no copy of it: a second, separately-written list is exactly
what drifted (never populated, so every reader saw zero scenarios and
the ship gate passed on an empty set). Records written before that
list was removed still deserialize; the stale key is ignored.

reopen.description:
Who reopened this subject from `shipped` to `verifying`, and why
(0.18 D3, `canon subject move <id> --to verifying --reason`). Set
only on the record that reopens; every other `canon subject
move` write clears it, like [`Self::status_override`]. Skipped
when absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

status_override.description:
The accountable waiver this record's status transition was let
through under, when `spec_coverage.require_review` refused it and
the operator passed `canon subject move --override-reason`.
Skipped when absent, so every subject written without one stays
byte-identical on the wire. Each `canon subject move` write
clears it and sets it again only when it waives something, so a
waiver never outlives the status it was granted for.

status_reason.description:
The note an operator gave the transition that wrote this record
(`canon subject move <id> --to <state> --reason`, 0.21.1), on
any transition; a reopen records it here too, next to
[`Self::reopen`]. Every `canon subject move` write clears it
and sets it again only when given a `--reason`. Skipped when
absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

StatusOverride.description:
A recorded waiver of the `spec_coverage.require_review` status guard
(see [`Subject::status_override`]). `canon gate check` reports a gap
as an advisory naming this waiver only when it matches one of
`waived` exactly, and only while the subject stays at `to`. A gap that
appears later (a new blocker, a newly tagged scenario) is not covered
and stays a violation.

reason.description: The operator's reason, verbatim (one line).

to.description: The status the transition moved to under this waiver.

waived.description: Exactly the guard violations this waiver let through, sorted.

actor.description: Who gave it.

reason.description: The operator's reason, verbatim (one line).

Subject.description:
A subject (join-spine `subject_id` row: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario)
— the durable product/management unit a team plans, designs, builds,
and measures across many changes (s36, the reviewed 13th kind). A
by-id kind like [`Change`]: flat Hive partition, no mandatory
`scenario_id`. `domain` is a validated-shape-only kebab slug (see
[`deserialize_domain_slug`] — the closed vocabulary lives in
`canon/vocab`, not here); `owner_role` names the accountable role;
`change_ids` accumulates as plan changes are adopted
(additive-empty by default, so a freshly-authored subject with no
links yet is still a valid, minimal record). One change may be listed
by several subjects (0.18 D4); the change's own
[`Change::subject_ids`] lists each of them, and readers join a
subject to its changes from both sides.

The scenario side of the join lives on [`Scenario::subject_id`], set
by `canon inventory sync` from each scenario's `@subject:<id>` tag —
the spec corpus is the one place that link is authored. A subject
carries no copy of it: a second, separately-written list is exactly
what drifted (never populated, so every reader saw zero scenarios and
the ship gate passed on an empty set). Records written before that
list was removed still deserialize; the stale key is ignored.

reopen.description:
Who reopened this subject from `shipped` to `verifying`, and why
(0.18 D3, `canon subject move <id> --to verifying --reason`). Set
only on the record that reopens; every other `canon subject
move` write clears it, like [`Self::status_override`]. Skipped
when absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

schema.description:
Per-kind FORMAT GENERATION — the value
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] defines and every writer stamps
via [`Envelope::current`] (design D2; `canon fmt`/`canon
migrate`, S11, key off it; `canon_store::fold::fold_latest_by_key`
orders an equal-`at` supersession tie by it,
`s38-evidence-bearing-memory`). See
[`RecordKind::schema_version`] for the bump rule — it is "bump
when two generations of one record can tie on `at`", not "bump on
every field addition".

status_override.description:
The accountable waiver this record's status transition was let
through under, when `spec_coverage.require_review` refused it and
the operator passed `canon subject move --override-reason`.
Skipped when absent, so every subject written without one stays
byte-identical on the wire. Each `canon subject move` write
clears it and sets it again only when it waives something, so a
waiver never outlives the status it was granted for.

status_reason.description:
The note an operator gave the transition that wrote this record
(`canon subject move <id> --to <state> --reason`, 0.21.1), on
any transition; a reopen records it here too, next to
[`Self::reopen`]. Every `canon subject move` write clears it
and sets it again only when given a `--reason`. Skipped when
absent, so every other subject stays byte-identical.

SubjectId.description: subject slug: kebab-case (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), the durable product-unit identifier — joins: subject ↔ change ↔ scenario

SubjectShowReport.description: `data` of the subject leaves: the Subject record, embedded verbatim (it keeps the ledger record's own schema and snake_case keys).
SubjectShowReport.title: SubjectReport

SubjectStatus.description:
A `Subject`'s lifecycle (s36 design D1): the states a product unit
moves through, `proposed → specced → building → verifying → shipped
→ retired`. Transitions are policy-gated (CEL) at the CLI/gate layer
(s35 seam); this enum owns only the closed set and its stable
snake_case wire spelling.

WaivedViolation.description:
One violation a [`StatusOverride`] let through: the gate failure
class (`unreviewed-promotion`, `open-blocker`) and the violation's
subject (a scenario id, or `<change_id>#<round>.<seq>` for a
blocker), as `canon gate check` prints them.

Actor.description:
Who/what produced a record — structured, never a bare `by: String`
(design D2, the donor audit's biggest cross-family gap).

`role` is `Option` (S11 design D5, "actor backfill is best-effort
from adjacent fields; absent stays absent"): a migrated legacy
record whose only source field is a bare `by: "legacy-ci-machine"`
string carries no role information at all — `canon migrate` maps
that string to `agent_id` and leaves `role: null` rather than
guessing, so the field must be able to express "unknown", not just
"known". Every record canon itself originates still supplies a role
via [`Actor::new`]; only backfilled/migrated records use
[`Actor::new_unattributed`].

retryable.description: True only where running the same command again can succeed; equal to the registry row's.

RecordKind.description:
The fourteen closed record kinds `canon-model` recognizes (design D1;
`Subject` is the reviewed 13th kind, added by s36, and `Finding` the
reviewed 14th, added by s43 — the "a new kind is a reviewed, breaking
`canon-model` change" process design D1 mandates, exercised twice for
real). A fifteenth kind is again a reviewed, breaking
change — never a `kind: String` escape hatch (design D1's explicitly
rejected alternative: an untyped `payload: serde_json::Value` would
silently recreate the "no documented join key" problem inside canon
itself).

errors.fix: Show the human what they approve (`canon brief show <change> --body` for a brief), ask with the harness question tool, and only on their explicit approval run the call again with --relayed-via <tool>, --actor, --approver and --note (a brief also takes --digest <change>=<shown digest>). Where canon.yaml says `approval: { relay: deny }`, the human runs the call in their own shell (or on the dashboard for a brief). Never remove your role (`env -u CANON_ROLE`, dropping --as) to run it yourself.
errors.meaning: this leaf records a human's decision (`brief approve`, `policy approve`, `divergence accept`, a `migrate --commit` that re-binds `Approved:` lines), so an agent role (planner, implementer, reviewer, orchestrator declared with --as or CANON_ROLE) is refused unless it relays the human's explicit answer with --relayed-via, and a repo whose canon.yaml says `approval: { relay: deny }` refuses that too

errors.fix: Have the adapter return a response that authorizes execution, or do not run the command through this adapter.
errors.meaning: `adapter authorize` read the response and its answer is that execution is not authorized: the check's negative answer, its result in data

errors.fix: Make the --response file readable by this user, then run the command again.
errors.meaning: the adapter response file exists but this user may not read it

errors.fix: Run `canon adapter validate --response <file>` to see which rule the response breaks, fix the response, then run the command again.
errors.meaning: the adapter response file cannot be used as a response: it is not a file or not UTF-8 text, or (for `adapter authorize`) it breaks a rule of the response envelope

errors.fix: Pass --response naming an existing response file.

errors.fix: Pass an --actor the allowed_signers file lists, or have the human add the actor's key to it and approve the policy (`canon policy approve`), then run `canon strategy rollback` again.
errors.meaning: the --actor of a `strategy rollback` is not listed in the policy's allowed_signers file, so it may not sign a rollback; nothing was recorded

errors.fix: Set `approval: { allowed_signers: <path> }` in .canon/policy.yaml and have the human approve it with `canon policy approve`, then run `canon strategy rollback` again.
errors.meaning: `.canon/policy.yaml` names no `approval.allowed_signers` verifier, so a `strategy rollback` cannot be checked; nothing was recorded

errors.fix: Get what error.details names (a human's approval of the brief, an independent review, evidence for the scenario), then run `canon subject move` again.
errors.meaning: the status transition needs an approval, a review or evidence the subject does not have; error.details names each cause when there are several, and nothing was written

errors.fix: Correct the malformed `canon subject` argument.
errors.meaning: a `subject` argument is malformed

errors.fix: Check the subject with `canon subject show` and request what its state allows.
errors.meaning: the requested change conflicts with the subject's state: a status transition that is not allowed, an unadopt of an approved or flow-tagged change

reasons.fix: Leave the change adopted, or unadopt only a change nobody approved.
reasons.meaning: the change carries an approved brief, which is the subject's approved scope, so it stays adopted

reasons.fix: Remove or retag the `@flow:<change>.*` tags on those scenarios first, then unadopt again.
reasons.meaning: a scenario the subject owns is tagged `@flow:<change>.*`, so unadopting the change would make it fall back to an older approval

reasons.fix: Check the subject's status with `canon subject show` and request an allowed transition.
reasons.meaning: the status change is not an allowed transition

errors.fix: Choose a different subject id, or use the existing subject (`canon subject show`).
errors.meaning: a subject with that id already exists

errors.fix: Fix each cause error.details names (the error itself when it names one), then run `canon subject move` again.
errors.meaning: the status transition breaks a rule of the gate that is not a missing approval, review or evidence; error.details names each cause when there are several

reasons.fix: Fix the behavior the audit refuted, re-attest it, record the evaluator's new audit (`canon evidence audit <SCENARIO_ID>`), then run `canon subject move` again.
reasons.meaning: a scenario the transition rests on has a latest audit that is `refuted`: an external evaluator found its declared success false, and a `faithful` verdict does not override it

reasons.fix: Fix or remove the record `error.details` names, then run `canon subject move` again.
reasons.meaning: a record the gate reads to judge the transition does not parse or lacks a required field, so it counts as no evidence and the gate fails closed

reasons.fix: Close the blocker finding (`canon finding close`) once it is fixed, then run `canon subject move` again.
reasons.meaning: an open `blocker` finding sits on a change the subject adopts, and the review policy blocks the transition on open findings

errors.fix: Pass the id of an existing subject; `canon status` lists the subjects.
errors.meaning: no subject with that id

errors.fix: Pass --reason when reopening a shipped subject with `canon subject move`.
errors.meaning: reopening a shipped subject needs --reason

errors.fix: Correct the task's evidence or typed atom named in the error, then run `canon task done` again.
errors.meaning: the evidence or typed atom for the task is invalid

errors.fix: Attach the evidence the task requires, then run `canon task done` again.
errors.meaning: `task done` refused to flip the task: its evidence does not support it

errors.fix: Pass a well-formed task id to `canon task done`.
errors.meaning: the task id is malformed

errors.fix: Pass a task id that exists in the plan corpus.
errors.meaning: the task id names no task in the plan corpus

errors.fix: Mark the task done by hand in the plan document; this plan dialect cannot be flipped by canon.
errors.meaning: the plan dialect cannot flip this task

errors.fix: Read the error message, fix its cause, then run tier aging again.
errors.meaning: tier aging failed before it moved any record, or a move failed and no record had left its tier

errors.fix: Read what was done first (the first `meta.next` step), fix the cause the error names, then preview with `canon tier age` and move the rest with `--commit --plan-digest <DIGEST>` (the same digest is stale now).
errors.meaning: tier aging stopped after it moved some records: what moved stays moved

reasons.fix: Read what was done (`canon status`), fix the cause the message names, then preview again with `canon tier age` and commit its new plan.
reasons.meaning: tier aging moved some records, then a later move failed; what moved stays moved

errors.fix: Wait a moment, check that the tier backends are reachable, then run tier aging again.
errors.meaning: tier aging could not read a tier before it moved any record: a tier backend whose settings are all there did not answer (a Postgres DSN that is set and cannot be reached), or the system failed the read of a file in a way a repeat can pass; nothing was moved

errors.fix: Pass more characters of the commit sha; `expected` lists the candidates.
errors.meaning: the sha prefix `trace` was given is the start of more than one commit

errors.fix: Pass the key of a finding (`canon query --kind finding`), a review id a review printed, or enough characters of a commit sha to name one commit.
errors.meaning: no record says the id `trace` was given

errors.fix: Pass a review id (26 characters), a commit sha (7 to 40 hex digits) or a finding key (`<change>_<round>_<seq>`).
errors.meaning: `trace` was given something that is none of a review id, a commit sha or a finding key (a placeholder node's id is not one)

errors.fix: Pass the id of a trajectory that exists, or omit the contradicting trajectory.
errors.meaning: the contradicting trajectory does not exist

errors.fix: Fix the change's typed-atoms file so it parses.
errors.meaning: the typed-atoms file for the change does not parse

errors.fix: Run one of the commands `expected` lists; `canon schema` lists every command path.
errors.meaning: a command word is not in canon's command tree, or `canon schema` was given a path canon does not have; `expected` lists the valid words at that level

errors.fix: Widen the check so it examines something; meta.coverage says what was looked at.
errors.meaning: a check examined nothing, so it cannot report clean: data.unverifiable is true and meta.coverage says what was looked at

errors.fix: Run the command with --help and correct the argument `field` names; `expected` lists the valid values when there is a closed set.
errors.meaning: the command line did not parse or breaks a constraint: an unknown option, a missing or malformed value, an unexpected operand, a `--fields` name that cannot be selected, `--input` given twice or without a value, `--input -` beside another option that reads stdin, a retrieval scoped by neither or both of `--regime` and `--domain`; `field` names the argument

errors.fix: Make the target writable (its permissions, a read-only mount), then run the command again.
errors.meaning: a target the command writes is read-only or this user may not write it, known before anything was changed; nothing was written

errors.fix: Check that the target path is writable and has space, then run the command again.
errors.meaning: a write began and failed: a file or ledger record could not be written after the command started changing things; what an earlier step wrote stays, and the message says which

errors.fix: Create the missing directory or name a directory that exists, then run the command again.
errors.meaning: a target the command writes cannot be a target: its directory is missing or is not a directory, known before anything was changed; nothing was written

exitTable.meaning: the command ran and its answer is negative or incomplete: a finding, a failed check, an unverifiable result, a failure after the work began, an internal error
the command refused to run: usage, an unknown command, CONFIG_REQUIRED, an id or file that does not exist, unreadable input, an invalid argument, a target that cannot be written

warnings.fix: Have the human approve the brief with `canon brief approve`, or take the adoption back with `canon subject unadopt`.

warnings.meaning: a task was flipped but its status record was not refreshed, so `canon query --kind task` may not match the plan

warnings.meaning: `CANON_ROLE` holds a value that is not a role and was ignored, because the command (`schema`, `context`, `skills show`) does not depend on the role
